{{short description|German mathematician}}
[[File:AndreasThom.jpg|thumb|right|Thom at [[Oberwolfach]], 2013]]

'''Andreas Thom''' is a German [[mathematician]], working on [[geometric group theory]], [[algebraic topology]], [[ergodic theory]] of group actions, and [[operator algebra]]s.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chair of Geometry|website=TU Dresden|url=https://tu-dresden.de/mn/math/geometrie/thom/forschung}}</ref>

==Education and career==

Thom received in 2000 his [[Certificate of Advanced Study in Mathematics]] from the [[University of Cambridge]]. In 2003 he obtained his doctorate ([[Promotion (Germany)|Promotion]]) from the [[University of Münster]] with thesis advisor [[Joachim Cuntz]] and thesis ''Connective E-Theory and Bivariant Homology for C*-Algebra''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=76127}}</ref> He was a Postdoc 2003–2005 at the University of Münster, and 2005–2007 at the [[University of Göttingen]]. From 2007 to 2009 he was a junior professor for ''Geometrical Aspects of Pure Mathematics'' at the University of Göttingen. After being promoted to assistant professor in Göttingen, he moved in 2009 to become a full professor for ''Theoretical Mathematics'' at the [[University of Leipzig]]. In 2014 he moved to a full professorship in geometry at [[TU Dresden]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Chair of Geometry|website=TU Dresden|url=https://tu-dresden.de/mn/math/geometrie/thom/die-professur/werdegang}}</ref>

His work with Gábor Kun laid the foundations for the discovery of a [[non-sofic group]]. Prior to this discovery their approach was not considered as the main line of attack on the problem, and approaches involving [[Quantum game theory|quantum games]] were considered more promising.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://finance.biggo.com/news/e25efed9-378a-4987-a29c-856268143b07|title=OpenAI's Math Breakthrough Hit by Fresh Plagiarism Storm: Dresden Mathematician Publishes Emails Alleging 20 Years of Work Was Stolen}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2026/09/11/on-the-existence-of-non-sofic-groups/|title=
On the existence of non-sofic groups}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==

* In 2011, Thom received an ERC Starting Grant No. 277728 ''Geometry and Analysis of Group Rings''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chair of Geometry|website=TU Dresden|url=https://tu-dresden.de/mn/math/geometrie/thom/die-professur/werdegang}}</ref>
* In 2016, he received an ERC Consolidator Grant No. 681207 ''Groups, Dynamics, and Approximation''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chair of Geometry|website=TU Dresden|url=https://tu-dresden.de/mn/math/geometrie/thom/die-professur/werdegang}}</ref>
* In 2018, Thom was an invited speaker for a talk ''Finitary approximations of groups and their applications'' at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Rio de Janeiro.
